dbIssues.failure_scenario: DATABASE_URL unset in dev (validateEnv skipped) → db.ts line 8 process.env.DATABASE_URL! yields undefined → `new pg.Pool({connectionString: undefined})` throws opaque TypeError at first DB access instead of a clear startup error
dbIssues.short_summary: Dev env validation skipped, non-null assertion hides missing DATABASE_URL
dbIssues.summary: validateEnv() only runs in production, so a missing DATABASE_URL in dev causes an opaque crash at first DB access rather than a clear startup error. The `!` assertion on line 8 produces no runtime guard.

dbIssues.failure_scenario: Postgres connection error returned in Arabic locale with msg 'انتهت مهلة الاتصال' → withRetry string checks fail → error surfaces as non-transient → no retry attempted
dbIssues.short_summary: withRetry string-matching misses locale-specific error messages
dbIssues.summary: withRetry detects transient errors via brittle substring matching on `.message` ("connection", "timeout", "deadlock", "500"). Localized or non-standard error messages bypass the retry logic entirely.

dbIssues.failure_scenario: MenuItem price = 0.0123456789 stored as Decimal → Number() in compute → truncated to ~0.01234568 → downstream math diverges from database value
dbIssues.short_summary: Prisma Decimal → Number loses precision on high-precision values
dbIssues.summary: The $extends block converts all Prisma Decimal fields to JavaScript Number. For currency values in this domain (prices/orders have ~2-4 decimal places) the precision loss is negligible, but this is an implicit semantic change from the DB schema type.

hookIssues.failure_scenario: useConfig() used while /api/config is down (network error, server 500) → .catch(() => {}) absorbs the error → config stays {} → consumers silently operate with empty defaults — broken delivery fee or feature flags with no user feedback
hookIssues.short_summary: Silent catch swallows all config fetch errors
hookIssues.summary: useConfig silently swallows all fetch errors via .catch(() => {}). Consumers cannot distinguish 'config fetched and empty' from 'config fetch failed' — both produce the same loaded=true + empty config object.

hookIssues.failure_scenario: Component using useConfig() unmounts before fetch resolves → setConfig/setLoaded fires on unmounted component → React state update warning (memory leak path in React <19)
hookIssues.short_summary: No AbortController, setState on unmount possible
hookIssues.summary: No AbortController or mounted ref guard. If the component unmounts before the fetch resolves, setConfig/setLoaded fire on an unmounted component (React state update warning).

hookIssues.failure_scenario: useConfig() used in 3 separate components → each fires its own independent GET /api/config → 3 network requests for the same data
hookIssues.short_summary: useConfig fires a new fetch per consumer with no dedup
hookIssues.summary: useConfig fires a new fetch from every component that calls it. No request deduplication, no cached response — N consumers = N identical fetches.

routingIssues.failure_scenario: admin/system-events page throws during render → no error.tsx in route segment → bubbles to parent admin/error.tsx → entire admin section loses its context (sidebar, navigation)
routingIssues.summary: admin/system-events has only loading.tsx, no error.tsx. While it inherits admin's error boundary, the error would take down the entire admin layout rather than just the affected route.

routingIssues.failure_scenario: Page load triggers preload of 3 custom woff2 fonts + Cairo via next/font/google → 4 font families compete for bandwidth → LCP delayed on slow connections
routingIssues.short_summary: Three custom fonts preloaded plus Cairo, up to 4 families
routingIssues.summary: Root layout preloads noto-naskh-arabic, noto-sans-arabic, and readex-pro woff2 files, plus Cairo via next/font/google. Four font families is heavy — likely only 2-3 are used per page view.

routingIssues.failure_scenario: <Analytics> from @vercel/analytics/react internally calls useSearchParams() in production build → no Suspense boundary above it → throws an error on dynamic-rendered routes
routingIssues.summary: <Analytics /> is rendered directly in the root layout with no wrapping <Suspense> boundary. Next.js requires Suspense around any component that calls useSearchParams() in production — if @vercel/analytics does so internally (its "/" script injection path does not, but its advanced modes may), this would throw.

storeIssues.failure_scenario: User loads cart page, items exist in localStorage from prior session → skipHydration prevents rehydrate → cart appears empty → user thinks order is lost, leaves frustrated
storeIssues.short_summary: skipHydration:true without manual rehydration — persisted cart never restores
storeIssues.summary: Zustand persist has skipHydration: true but no component ever calls useCart.persist.rehydrate(). Cart data IS written to localStorage on every state change, but is NEVER read back on page reload. Cart is effectively session-only.

storeIssues.failure_scenario: totalItems() / subtotal() called via get() inside store → each call creates a new store subscription → unnecessary re-renders on the calling component when unrelated state fields change
storeIssues.short_summary: totalItems/subtotal use get() creating full-store subscriptions
storeIssues.summary: totalItems() and subtotal() use get().items inside the store rather than being selectors. Consumers calling these get the entire store's state, re-rendering on any change rather than only on item changes.
